clauses.title: PROBATION
clauses.plain_english: You will be on probation for 6 months. During this period, the company has the right to terminate your employment by giving 15 days' notice or paying 15 days' salary in lieu of notice.
clauses.exact_quote: You will be on probation for a period of 6 months. During this period, the company may terminate your employment by giving 15 days of notice or salary in lieu thereof.
clauses.concern_rationale: This is a standard probation clause. Termination during probation is typically easier for the employer than after confirmation, often with a shorter notice period.

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Termination by company during probation period
consequence_steps: The company may provide 15 days' advance notice of termination.
Alternatively, the company may pay you 15 days' salary instead of providing notice.

clauses.title: NOTICE PERIOD
clauses.plain_english: After your probation is successfully completed and your employment is confirmed, either you or the company can terminate the employment agreement by giving 60 days' written notice.
clauses.exact_quote: After confirmation, either party may terminate this agreement by providing 60 days of written notice.
clauses.concern_rationale: This is a standard reciprocal notice period clause. A 60-day notice period is common in many professional employment contracts in India.

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Employee resigns without providing 60 days' notice
consequence_steps: The employee may be liable to pay salary in lieu of the unserved notice period.
The company typically has the right to adjust any amount owed from the employee's final settlement, which may include salary, gratuity, or other benefits.
consequence_scenarios.financial_estimate: Up to 60 days of your salary

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Company terminates employment without providing 60 days' notice
consequence_steps: The company may be liable to pay salary in lieu of the unserved notice period to the employee.
The employee typically receives this payment as part of their final settlement.
consequence_scenarios.financial_estimate: Up to 60 days of your salary

clauses.title: COMMITMENT BOND
clauses.plain_english: Due to significant company investment in your specialized training, you are required to remain employed for a minimum of 18 months from your joining date. If you resign before this 18-month period, you will be liable to pay the company INR 2,00,000 as liquidated damages for training costs.
clauses.exact_quote: The company will invest significantly in your specialized training. Therefore, you agree to remain in the employment of the company for a minimum period of 18 months from your joining date. If you resign before this period, you shall be liable to pay the company a sum of INR 2,00,000 as liquidated damages to cover training costs.
clauses.concern_rationale: Service bonds are common but can be legally challenged. While enforceable, the liquidated damages amount (INR 2,00,000) must be a genuine pre-estimate of loss and not a penalty. Courts often scrutinize such clauses to ensure fairness.

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Resignation before completing the 18-month commitment period
consequence_steps: The employee may be liable to pay INR 2,00,000 to the company as liquidated damages.
The company typically has the right to recover this amount, potentially by adjusting it from the employee's final settlement or by initiating legal proceedings.
The enforceability of the full INR 2,00,000 may depend on whether it truly reflects the actual, verifiable training costs or if a court deems it to be a penalty.

clauses.title: NON-COMPETE
clauses.plain_english: For a period of 12 months after your employment with TechCorp ends, you are restricted from joining any direct competitor of the company in the fintech sector within India.
clauses.exact_quote: For a period of 12 months after leaving the company, you shall not join any direct competitor of TechCorp in the fintech space within India.
clauses.concern_rationale: Post-employment non-compete clauses are largely unenforceable in India under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, as they are considered to be in restraint of trade. Courts generally strike down such clauses unless they are narrowly tailored to protect specific trade secrets or goodwill and are reasonable. A broad restriction 'within India' is particularly vulnerable.

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Employee joins a direct competitor in the fintech space within 12 months of leaving TechCorp
consequence_steps: The company may attempt to seek an injunction from a court to prevent your employment with the competitor.
The company may also pursue damages for alleged breach of contract, though successful claims for damages in such cases are rare.

However, such clauses are largely unenforceable in India, and courts typically do not uphold them unless they are proven to protect specific, verifiable trade secrets or goodwill and are deemed reasonable and not merely a restraint of trade.
consequence_scenarios.financial_estimate: Potential legal costs if disputed; damages are uncertain and typically not awarded for simple breach of non-compete.

clauses.title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
clauses.plain_english: All intellectual property, including code and inventions, that you create during your employment period will belong exclusively to the company.
clauses.exact_quote: All intellectual property, code, and inventions created by you during your employment shall be the exclusive property of the company.
clauses.concern_rationale: This is a standard and generally enforceable clause in employment contracts, particularly for roles involving creation of intellectual property. It aligns with Indian IP laws where creations by an employee in the course of employment typically belong to the employer.

consequence_scenarios.trigger: Employee claims ownership or uses intellectual property created during employment for personal gain or a competitor
consequence_steps: The company may initiate legal action to assert its ownership rights over the intellectual property.
The employee may be required to formally assign all relevant IP rights to the company.
There may be liability for damages if the IP was used to the company's detriment.
consequence_scenarios.financial_estimate: Potential legal costs and damages, depending on the nature and value of the IP and the extent of its unauthorized use.
